k: Revive and heal the party.
src: 'Revive and heal the party.'

k: Eight shots, all at once.
src: 'Eight shots, all at once.'

k: The three of Lanternfall.
src: 'The three of Lanternfall.'

k: Everything you've been through, together.
src: 'Everything you\'ve been through, together.'

k: THE BELLRING — CUPS TODAYnCOPPER · SILVER · GOLD · SUNSTEELnChampion: VALKA THE UNDEFEATED (41–0)nThe management patches all contenders. The management is not liable for pride.
src:
'THE BELLRING — CUPS TODAY
COPPER · SILVER · GOLD · SUNSTEEL
Champion: VALKA THE UNDEFEATED (41–0)
The management patches all contenders. The management is not liable for pride.'

k: Cups
src: 'Cups'

k: Prizes
src: 'Prizes'

k: I've seen Valka fight forty-one times.
src: 'I\'ve seen Valka fight forty-one times.'

k: I've lost money forty-one times. I keep betting against her. It's a principle now.
src: 'I\'ve lost money forty-one times. I keep betting against her. It\'s a principle now.'

k: When the bell rings, the whole city stops. Even the Cathedral bells wait for ours.
src: 'When the bell rings, the whole city stops. Even the Cathedral bells wait for ours.'

k: Don't tell the Choir I said that.
src: 'Don\'t tell the Choir I said that.'

k: The Iron Bull was cast from a cracked bell. If you hit it right, it still rings.
src: 'The Iron Bull was cast from a cracked bell. If you hit it right, it still rings.'

k: Nobody has hit it right.
src: 'Nobody has hit it right.'

k: Kell the Net and Kell the Fist are brothers. Kell the Third sells the pies.
src: 'Kell the Net and Kell the Fist are brothers. Kell the Third sells the pies.'

k: The pies are the most dangerous thing here.
src: 'The pies are the most dangerous thing here.'

k: Between rounds we give you back a quarter of your strength. Any more and Mr. Brass says it isn't sport.
src: 'Between rounds we give you back a quarter of your strength. Any more and Mr. Brass says it isn\'t sport.'

k: Lose a cup and we patch everything. Free. It's the only free thing in Aurenne.
src: 'Lose a cup and we patch everything. Free. It\'s the only free thing in Aurenne.'

k: Honey-buns! Fresh from the oven! Still warm — they're always still warm!
src: 'Honey-buns! Fresh from the oven! Still warm — they\'re always still warm!'

k: ...She said that exact same thing. *Exactly* the same.
src: '...She said that exact same thing. *Exactly* the same.'

k: Same pitch. Same breath in the same place.
src: 'Same pitch. Same breath in the same place.'

k: Honey-buns! Fresh from the— fresh from the— Still warm. Still warm. Still warm.
src: 'Honey-buns! Fresh from the— fresh from the— Still warm. Still warm. Still warm.'

k: Look how high it goes! Mama, look! Look how high it goes!
src: 'Look how high it goes! Mama, look! Look how high it goes!'

k: There isn't a kite. He's holding nothing.
src: 'There isn\'t a kite. He\'s holding nothing.'

k: Yes, love. Very high.
src: 'Yes, love. Very high.'

k: She's not looking at him. She's looking at the wrong bit of sky. Forty years, the wrong bit of sky.
src: 'She\'s not looking at him. She\'s looking at the wrong bit of sky. Forty years, the wrong bit of sky.'

k: And-a-one, and-a-two, and-a—
src: 'And-a-one, and-a-two, and-a—'

k: Play it! Just *play* it!
src: 'Play it! Just *play* it!'

k: And-a-one, and-a-two, and-a-one, and-a-two, and-a-one, and-a-two, and-a—
src: 'And-a-one, and-a-two, and-a-one, and-a-two, and-a-one, and-a-two, and-a—'

k: _(her bow hovers a hair above the strings, trembling, waiting for the count)_
src: '_(her bow hovers a hair above the strings, trembling, waiting for the count)_'

k: The Lantern's humming oddly. I'll look at it after the festival. There's always time after the festival.
src: 'The Lantern\'s humming oddly. I\'ll look at it after the festival. There\'s always time after the festival.'

k: He doesn't know. He'll never know. He'll never get to tonight.
src: 'He doesn\'t know. He\'ll never know. He\'ll never get to tonight.'

k: The Keeper says it's probably the heat. Probably the heat. It's a very hot day.
src: 'The Keeper says it\'s probably the heat. Probably the heat. It\'s a very hot day.'

k: You're the Gloam! You have to catch us before the sun goes down!
src: 'You\'re the Gloam! You have to catch us before the sun goes down!'

k: ...I played this. In the window. Every day.
src: '...I played this. In the window. Every day.'

k: But the sun never goes down! Ha ha! The sun never goes down!
src: 'But the sun never goes down! Ha ha! The sun never goes down!'

k: Don't laugh like that. Don't— just don't.
src: 'Don\'t laugh like that. Don\'t— just don\'t.'

k: Your future, dear? Oh — there isn't one. Isn't that wonderful?
src: 'Your future, dear? Oh — there isn\'t one. Isn\'t that wonderful?'

k: She looked at me. She actually *looked* at me.
src: 'She looked at me. She actually *looked* at me.'

k: You're not from today, are you. Sister Mercy knows you're here. She knew before you did.
src: 'You\'re not from today, are you. Sister Mercy knows you\'re here. She knew before you did.'

k: Some day I'll be a knight. A real one. The kind that doesn't run.
src: 'Some day I\'ll be a knight. A real one. The kind that doesn\'t run.'

k: That's him. That's Sir Aldous. He's— he's younger than *me*.
src: 'That\'s him. That\'s Sir Aldous. He\'s— he\'s younger than *me*.'

k: You will be. You were. You were the best one.
src: 'You will be. You were. You were the best one.'

k: _(quietly)_ And you ran, once. Back for me. That's the only running you ever did.
src: '_(quietly)_ And you ran, once. Back for me. That\'s the only running you ever did.'

k: Have you seen my Lysa? She was just here. She's wearing her festival dress — white and gold, with a ribbon.
src: 'Have you seen my Lysa? She was just here. She\'s wearing her festival dress — white and gold, with a ribbon.'

k: ...She asks every hour. I used to answer her.
src: '...She asks every hour. I used to answer her.'

k: Have you seen my— have you seen— she was just here. She was just here. She was just here.
src: 'Have you seen my— have you seen— she was just here. She was just here. She was just here.'

k: Lovely day for it!
src: 'Lovely day for it!'

k: For *what*, friend?
src: 'For *what*, friend?'

k: ...Yeah. That's what I figured.
src: '...Yeah. That\'s what I figured.'

k: Lovely day for— lovely day for— lovely day for—
src: 'Lovely day for— lovely day for— lovely day for—'

k: Welcome to the Festival of the Long Light. Enjoy the day.
src: 'Welcome to the Festival of the Long Light. Enjoy the day.'

k: Enjoy the day. Enjoy the day. Enjoy the day.
src: 'Enjoy the day. Enjoy the day. Enjoy the day.'

k: The fountain. Its water arcs up and hangs at the top of the arc, glittering, and does not come down.
src: 'The fountain. Its water arcs up and hangs at the top of the arc, glittering, and does not come down.'

k: Trays of honey-buns, glazed and golden. They are warm. They have been warm for forty years.
src: 'Trays of honey-buns, glazed and golden. They are warm. They have been warm for forty years.'

k: Nobody has ever eaten one.
src: 'Nobody has ever eaten one.'

k: The Cathedral doors are painted on. There is no inside. He never went in that day.
src: 'The Cathedral doors are painted on. There is no inside. He never went in that day.'

k: The Grand Lantern, humming oddly in the heat. Its light is the color of honey. It will fail tonight. It never gets to.
src: 'The Grand Lantern, humming oddly in the heat. Its light is the color of honey. It will fail tonight. It never gets to.'

k: A cherry tree in full bloom. Petals fall from it constantly, turning in the air — and never land.
src: 'A cherry tree in full bloom. Petals fall from it constantly, turning in the air — and never land.'

k: The river doesn't flow. It glitters in place, every ripple exactly where it was.
src: 'The river doesn\'t flow. It glitters in place, every ripple exactly where it was.'

k: The vanity. A hairbrush with long black hairs in it, and a jar of ribbons, white and gold.
src: 'The vanity. A hairbrush with long black hairs in it, and a jar of ribbons, white and gold.'

k: Lysa's bed. Under the pillow, a list in a child's hand: THINGS TO DO WHEN I AM GROWN UP. The list is very long.
src: 'Lysa\'s bed. Under the pillow, a list in a child\'s hand: THINGS TO DO WHEN I AM GROWN UP. The list is very long.'

k: Picture books. One is open to a drawing of an animal with a glossy black coat. Under it, in careful letters: SABLE.
src: 'Picture books. One is open to a drawing of an animal with a glossy black coat. Under it, in careful letters: SABLE.'

k: A shelf of paper stars, each with a wish written inside. Most of them are about fireworks.
src: 'A shelf of paper stars, each with a wish written inside. Most of them are about fireworks.'

k: You came out. Nobody comes out.
src: 'You came out. Nobody comes out.'

k: ...Was he there? A boy, nine, with a gap in his teeth? Tam. His name is Tam.
src: '...Was he there? A boy, nine, with a gap in his teeth? Tam. His name is Tam.'

k: No. Don't tell me. I've decided I'm going home.
src: 'No. Don\'t tell me. I\'ve decided I\'m going home.'

k: My boy is in there. Tam. He was nine.
src: 'My boy is in there. Tam. He was nine.'

k: The Choir says when the Hierophant's work is done the gate will open, and I'll see him at the festival. I've been waiting since the spring.
src: 'The Choir says when the Hierophant\'s work is done the gate will open, and I\'ll see him at the festival. I\'ve been waiting since the spring.'

k: Is it still spring? I've lost count. Nothing changes up here. That's the point, they say.
src: 'Is it still spring? I\'ve lost count. Nothing changes up here. That\'s the point, they say.'

k: Eleven months I've sat here. My Marigold is inside. Forty-one years married.
src: 'Eleven months I\'ve sat here. My Marigold is inside. Forty-one years married.'

k: Some nights I can hear her laughing, through the wall. Same laugh. Same moment. Over and over.
src: 'Some nights I can hear her laughing, through the wall. Same laugh. Same moment. Over and over.'

k: I tell myself that's a comfort.
src: 'I tell myself that\'s a comfort.'

k: They say inside it's always the best day of your life. Isn't that what we all want? Isn't that what everyone has ever wanted?
src: 'They say inside it\'s always the best day of your life. Isn\'t that what we all want? Isn\'t that what everyone has ever wanted?'

k: I wanted my patients to get better. "Better" means "different." It means tomorrow.
src: 'I wanted my patients to get better. "Better" means "different." It means tomorrow.'

k: ...You sound very tired.
src: '...You sound very tired.'

k: I am. That's how I know I'm still alive.
src: 'I am. That\'s how I know I\'m still alive.'

k: You beat the Lift-Warden? He took my slingshot once. Did you get it back? ...No? Well. Still.
src: 'You beat the Lift-Warden? He took my slingshot once. Did you get it back? ...No? Well. Still.'

k: The big gate never opens. Don't bother knocking; I knocked for a week.
src: 'The big gate never opens. Don\'t bother knocking; I knocked for a week.'

k: But the white ships bring crates round the east side of the plaza. There's a lift. A man with a spear stands by it and says "halt" a lot.
src: 'But the white ships bring crates round the east side of the plaza. There\'s a lift. A man with a spear stands by it and says "halt" a lot.'
